message.content:
In the repo /home/nick/work/andesim, map the CURRENT test coverage of the `runtime/linux` component (the "vlinux" M-mode proxy kernel: main.c, loader.c, stack.c, mm.c, syscall.c, manifest.h, vlinux.ld, vlinux_mem.h).

Be thorough. I need these facts:

1. Every existing test that touches vlinux: list each file under tests/vlinux/, tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh, and any fixture under tests/fixtures/rt_linux_*. For each, one line: what behavior it asserts, and which mode(s)/engine(s) it runs in (fast / cycle / hybrid, qemu vs vsim).
2. How these tests are wired into the runner scripts: scripts/test_all.sh, scripts/run_e2e.sh, scripts/build_all.sh. Which phase runs tests/vlinux/*? Are they run by default? Is there a lint phase that checks for orphaned tests?
3. The full syscall surface implemented in runtime/linux/syscall.c: list every syscall number/name it dispatches, and mark which ones are exercised by an existing test vs untested. Include the ecall_hook / ROI interaction.
4. Whether ANY host-side unit tests exist for runtime/linux logic (e.g. the "host-testable RAM math" mentioned in commit 1a44ca1, mm.c arena math, vlinux_mem.h). Where do they live, what framework, how are they run?
5. Any roadmap/docs file describing runtime/linux status and known gaps (look for ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md and docs/USER_GUIDE.md sections). Summarize the phase list (U0..U11, X*) with done/parked/planned state, quoting the exact status markers.

Report as concise structured lists, with file:line references. Do not modify anything.

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

   5 # cannot exercise (its own fixture is -nostdlib, no libc at all).

   8 # fflush + exit(42) -- deterministic output (no printed pointers), so the
   9 # test can match it exactly, plus the specific exit code.
  10 #
  11 # KNOWN GAP (documented in the roadmap's U4 DONE note, not yet fixed):
  12 # glibc's exit() walks its internal atexit/on_exit/cxa_atexit handler list
  13 # before the real exit_group syscall; one handler registered by glibc's own
  14 # startup (very likely _dl_fini's internal __cxa_atexit registration) has a
  15 # garbage function pointer on THIS vendor riscv64 toolchain and faults when
  16 # called (illegal instruction, mcause=2). Confirmed NOT a vlinux bug: every
  17 # syscall vlinux answers (brk/mmap/write/uname/getrandom/...) is proven
  18 # correct by the SAME test up to that point, and by a parallel `_exit(42)`
  19 # build (bypasses the handler walk) that runs perfectly end to end, exact
  20 # output and exit code, on both legs. Confirmed via live comparison against
  21 # a native x86-64 glibc build that this handler slot is supposed to be
  22 # pointer-mangled (rotate+xor a per-process TLS-relative guard) before the
  23 # call; the riscv64 disassembly has no such de-mangle step at the call site
  24 # -- a toolchain-internals question, not something vlinux's own code can
  25 # fix. This test therefore accepts EITHER a clean exit 42 (if a future
  26 # toolchain/investigation fixes this) OR this exact, verified crash
  27 # signature -- anything else is a real (possibly new) failure and still
  28 # fails the test.

  31 # toolchain -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, like the rv32 fixtures need

   1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # U3 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): vlinux reads the app ELF named by
   3 # its manifest (g_manifest.app_path, U2), maps its PT_LOAD segments, builds
   4 # the Linux initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and jumps to the app entry
   5 # in M-mode. Proved with tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf (a -nostdlib
   6 # fixture -- no glibc needed yet, that's U4): it reads argv/auxv straight off
   7 # sp and echoes argv[0] + AT_PAGESZ via raw ecalls, which exercises U3's
   8 # minimal 2-syscall (write, exit_group) dispatch too.
   9 #
  10 # Two legs, same staged artifact (U1's dual-engine pattern): `andesim run
  11 # --mode fast --runtime linux` builds+boots the manifested vlinux-run.elf for
  12 # the fast leg and prints its staged path; that SAME staged ELF is then run
  13 # directly on the cycle engine (--mode cycle --runtime linux is not wired
  14 # until later -- ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U2's scope note).
  15 #
  16 # U8 addition: `-- extra args` after the app ELF thread through as
  17 # argv[1..] (deferred by U2/U3, needed once U8's real invocation --
  18 # `llama-completion -- -m model.gguf -t 1` -- has actual flags to pass).
  19 set -uo pipefail
  20 
  21 SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
  22 ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
  23 . "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
  24 
  25 TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
  26 [ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
  27 export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"
  28 
  29 require_driver
  30 [ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
  31 
  32 make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
  33 [ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"
  34 
  35 make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_argv.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"
  36 APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_argv.elf"
  37 [ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"
  38 
  39 SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  40 [ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
  41 
  42 # 1. fast leg: real run (not --dry-run) -- loader + stack + auxv + the app's
  43 #    own ecalls all execute for real. "-- extra1 extra2 extra3" (3 extras)
  44 #    must land as argv[1..3] (U8), not be silently dropped (U2/U3's old
  45 #    behavior). argc==4 here is EVEN -- deliberately, not argc==1's odd
  46 #    parity: the fixed auxv/envp/argv/argc block's size is a multiple of
  47 #    16 only for odd argc (see stack.c), so an even argc is the one that
  48 #    actually exercises the new alignment-padding branch. A real
  49 #    llama.cpp invocation (U8's actual target) also lands on an even argc,
  50 #    so this parity matters, not just argc==1's original coincidence.
  51 out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" -- extra1 extra2 extra3 2>&1); rc=$?
  52 [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast run exit $rc: $out"
  53 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "argv[0]=$APP" \
  54   || fail "fast: missing argv[0]=$APP in: $out"
  55 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[1]=extra1' \
  56   || fail "fast: missing argv[1]=extra1 in: $out"
  57 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[2]=extra2' \
  58   || fail "fast: missing argv[2]=extra2 in: $out"
  59 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[3]=extra3' \
  60   || fail "fast: missing argv[3]=extra3 in: $out"
  61 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'AT_PAGESZ=4096' \
  62   || fail "fast: missing AT_PAGESZ=4096 in: $out"
  63 ok "fast --runtime linux: loader + stack + auxv + 2-syscall dispatch (argv[0..3], even argc, + AT_PAGESZ echoed)"
  64 
  65 # 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly on the cycle
  66 #    engine (proves the loader/stack/dispatch code is engine-blind, like
  67 #    every other vlinux/vplat mechanism).
  68 vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
  69 [ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  70   || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"
  71 
  72 out=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
  73 [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle run exit $rc: $out"
  74 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "argv[0]=$APP" \
  75   || fail "cycle: missing argv[0]=$APP in: $out"
  76 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[1]=extra1' \
  77   || fail "cycle: missing argv[1]=extra1 in: $out"
  78 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF 'argv[2]=extra2' \
  79   || fail "cycle: missing argv[2]=extra2 in: $out"
  80 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'AT_PAGESZ=4096' \
  81   || fail "cycle: missing AT_PAGESZ=4096 in: $out"
  82 ok "cycle: the same staged vlinux-run.elf boots and runs the app identically (argv[0..2])"

1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # U2 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): `andesim run --mode fast --runtime
   3 # linux app.elf -- <app argv>` stages a manifested vlinux.elf (this run's app
   4 # path + mem-size stamped into its .manifest section via objcopy) and boots
   5 # THAT under -bios, instead of the app ELF directly.
   6 #
   7 # Scope: --mode fast (U2) and --mode hybrid (U9, case 6) are wired; cycle
   8 # is rejected (case 5 -- never wired, no roadmap need). App argv (-- ...) threads
   9 # into the manifest as argv[1..] (U8) -- this dry-run test proves the
  10 # objcopy step + manifest app-path AND argv round-trip, matching the
  11 # roadmap's Input/Output contract.

  13

  16 . "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
  17

  19 [ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
  20 export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

  29       || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  30 [ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"
  31 
  32 # 1. dry-run contract: objcopy step printed, -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf,
  33 #    engine-synced CPU, the 1G mem-size default, qemu itself stays a preview.
  34 out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux --dry-run "$elf" \
  35       -- -m x.gguf -t 1 2>&1); rc=$?
  36 [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run exit $rc: $out"
  37 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy' \
  38   || fail "missing the objcopy step: $out"
  39 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--update-section .manifest=' \
  40   || fail "missing --update-section .manifest=: $out"
  41 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \

  43 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '-bios [^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' \
  44   || fail "missing -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf: $out"
  45 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-m 1024M' \

  47 printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512' \
  48   || fail "missing the engine-synced CPU override: $out"

   1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # U4 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a REAL static-glibc binary reaches
   3 # main(), works, and exits cleanly under vlinux -- the syscall core (M-mode
   4 # ecall dispatch + brk/mmap-backed malloc) that U3's loader/stack alone
   5 # cannot exercise (its own fixture is -nostdlib, no libc at all).
   6 #
   7 # tests/fixtures/rt_linux_glibc_hello.c: argv + malloc(1MiB) + printf +
   8 # fflush + exit(42) -- deterministic output (no printed pointers), so the
   9 # test can match it exactly, plus the specific exit code.
  10 #
  11 # KNOWN GAP (documented in the roadmap's U4 DONE note, not yet fixed):
  12 # glibc's exit() walks its internal atexit/on_exit/cxa_atexit handler list
  13 # before the real exit_group syscall; one handler registered by glibc's own
  14 # startup (very likely _dl_fini's internal __cxa_atexit registration) has a
  15 # garbage function pointer on THIS vendor riscv64 toolchain and faults when
  16 # called (illegal instruction, mcause=2). Confirmed NOT a vlinux bug: every
  17 # syscall vlinux answers (brk/mmap/write/uname/getrandom/...) is proven
  18 # correct by the SAME test up to that point, and by a parallel `_exit(42)`
  19 # build (bypasses the handler walk) that runs perfectly end to end, exact
  20 # output and exit code, on both legs. Confirmed via live comparison against
  21 # a native x86-64 glibc build that this handler slot is supposed to be
  22 # pointer-mangled (rotate+xor a per-process TLS-relative guard) before the
  23 # call; the riscv64 disassembly has no such de-mangle step at the call site
  24 # -- a toolchain-internals question, not something vlinux's own code can
  25 # fix. This test therefore accepts EITHER a clean exit 42 (if a future
  26 # toolchain/investigation fixes this) OR this exact, verified crash
  27 # signature -- anything else is a real (possibly new) failure and still
  28 # fails the test.
  29 #
  30 # Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env), the vendor static-glibc
  31 # toolchain -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, like the rv32 fixtures need
  32 # HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32. Two legs, same staged artifact (U1/U3's pattern).
  33 set -uo pipefail
  34 
  35 SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
  36 ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
  37 . "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
  38 
  39 TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
  40 [ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
  41 export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"
  42 
  43 LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
  44 if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  45   ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  46   exit 0
  47 fi
  48 
  49 require_driver
  50 [ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
  51 
  52 make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
  53 [ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"
  54 
  55 make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  56   || fail "glibc fixture build failed"
  57 APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf"
  58 [ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"
  59 
  60 SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  61 [ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
  62 
  63 EXPECT="argv[0]=$APP malloc=ok"
  64 
  65 # Accept a clean exit 42 (full pass) OR the exact known exit()-handler crash
  66 # signature (stdout still correct -- the crash is strictly after the real
  67 # work finishes). Anything else -- wrong/missing output, or a different rc
  68 # -- is a real failure, known gap or not.
  69 check_leg() {
  70   local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
  71   printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$EXPECT" \
  72     || fail "$label: missing '$EXPECT' in: $out"
  73   if [ "$rc" -eq 42 ]; then
  74     ok "$label: static glibc reaches main(), malloc works, exit() cleanup ok (42)"
  75   elif [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'mcause: 0x2'; then
  76     ok "$label: static glibc reaches main(), malloc works; exit() handler-list crash is the known, documented gap (see ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4)"
  77   else
  78     fail "$label: exit $rc is neither clean (42) nor the known crash signature: $out"
  79   fi
  80 }
  81 
  82 # 1. fast leg.
  83 out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
  84 check_leg "fast" "$rc" "$out"
  85 
  86 # 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly. A full static
  87 #    glibc startup (TLS setup, IFUNC-ish riscv_hwprobe loop, malloc/mmap,
  88 #    stdio) is a lot more instructions than U1/U3's lighter fixtures --
  89 #    measured at ~7 minutes wall-clock on this host's vsim (~8 kHz); 600s
  90 #    gives headroom without being open-ended.
  91 vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
  92 [ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
  93   || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"
  94 
  95 out=$(timeout 600 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
  96 check_leg "cycle" "$rc" "$out"

   1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # U8 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a real static-glibc llama.cpp
   3 # binary (llama-completion) generates real text from Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf

   8 #   1. LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- the vendor static-glibc toolchain.
   9 #   2. A static riscv64 build of llama-completion at
  10 #      $LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN (default: $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/
  11 #      llama-completion) -- see docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 for the exact
  12 #      cmake recipe. Building it here would make an ordinary test run take
  13 #      many minutes; it is a one-time setup step, not a per-run cost.
  14 #   3. The Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf model at $BONSAI_GGUF (default:
  15 #      $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf).

  19 # total under QEMU's functional (not accelerated) RVV emulation -- real
  20 # matrix math on a real 4B-parameter model is slow here by design (fast
  21 # mode trades cycle accuracy for pure functional correctness, not speed).
  22 # -n 32 (the roadmap's own example) scales roughly linearly with token
  23 # count; 2400s gives ample headroom.
  24 #
  25 # --mem-size 2G (not the --runtime linux default of 1G): the model's own
  26 # mmap (572 MB) plus its KV cache buffer (576 MB at -c 512) exceeds 1G:
  27 # discovered by direct measurement, not assumed from the roadmap's
  28 # original (too optimistic) "1G covers it" estimate.
  29 #
  30 # Known gap (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4): glibc's exit() may crash in
  31 # its handler-list walk AFTER all real work (generation, perf stats) is
  32 # already complete and printed -- same documented, non-vlinux gap every
  33 # U4+ glibc test already accepts. This test checks for it explicitly so
  34 # a DIFFERENT failure still fails the test.

  53 GGUF="${BONSAI_GGUF:-$LLAMA_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}"

  56   exit 0

  62

  71   "$BIN" -- -m "$GGUF" -no-cnv --prompt "The capital of France is" \
  72   -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 2>&1); rc=$?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   lint      tests/test_*.sh + roi.test.sh + the fixture ROI-content lint
#             (fast harness self-checks; no engine spawns. The one heavy
#             harness test, tests/test_kernel_cycles.sh, stays manual: it
#             runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips the e2e phase already covers.)
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_lint() {
  step "[lint] harness self-checks"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/test_*.sh (each; kernel_cycles excluded)" \
      "tests/lib/roi.test.sh" "tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/test_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    # Heavy manual smoke test (real QEMU+vsim runs); e2e covers the surface.
    [ "$(basename "$s")" = "test_kernel_cycles.sh" ] && continue
    run_case "[lint] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
  run_case "[lint] roi.test.sh" bash "$ROOT/tests/lib/roi.test.sh"
  run_case "[lint] test_fixture_roi_content.sh" \
    bash "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return
  fi
  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)" \
      "tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh \
           "$ROOT"/tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    lint)     run_lint ;;
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
3	# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
4	#
5	# Env overrides:
6	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
7	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
8	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium,
9	#                falling back to the first sim_* only when the canonical
10	#                engine is not built -- see the comment at the default)
11	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
12	#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
13	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
14	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
15	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
16	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
17	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
18	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
19	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
20	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
21	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
22	
23	set -euo pipefail
24	
25	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
26	
27	# Fill env gaps from ./config.env (the per-host file setup.sh maintains) so
28	# `scripts/test_all.sh e2e` works from a fresh shell. An exported value wins;
29	# the file only supplies what the caller's shell lacks -- same pattern as
30	# tests/lib. Exported for the child builds (make -C tests/fixtures).
31	cfg_val() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -1; }
32	for _k in QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 \
33	          LINUX_TOOLCHAIN; do
34	  if [[ -z "${!_k:-}" ]]; then
35	    _v="$(cfg_val "$_k")"
36	    [[ -n "$_v" ]] && export "$_k=$_v"
37	  fi
38	done
39	unset _k _v
40	
41	# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
42	# VSIM_QEMU); empty when neither setup.sh nor config.env supplied it -- the
43	# require below reports it.
44	VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
45	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
46	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
47	
48	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
49	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
50	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
51	  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
52	  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
53	  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
54	  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
55	  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
56	  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
57	  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
58	  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
59	    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
60	  fi
61	fi
62	
63	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
64	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
65	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
66	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
67	
68	require() {
69	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
70	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
71	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
72	    exit 1
73	  fi
74	}
75	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
76	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
77	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
78	
79	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
80	
81	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
82	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
83	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
84	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
85	RT_TESTS=(
86	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
87	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
88	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
89	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
90	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
91	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
92	  "rt_all_fprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_fprs"
93	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
94	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
95	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
96	  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
97	  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
98	  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
99	  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
100	  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
101	  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
102	  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
103	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
104	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
105	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
106	  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
107	  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
108	  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
109	  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
110	  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
111	)
112	
113	NEG_TESTS=(
114	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
115	  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
116	  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
117	)
118	
119	# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
120	# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
121	# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
122	# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
123	# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
124	# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
125	# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
126	# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
127	SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
128	  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
129	  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
130	)
131	
132	# Fixture auto-build gate: the required ELF set is DERIVED from the test
133	# tables above (each entry's FIXTURE= token), so it cannot drift from the
134	# tests that consume the ELFs. The NEG_TESTS drivers reuse fixtures
135	# already named in RT_TESTS (handoff_roundtrip, rt_c_dlm_data,
136	# rt_c_hvm_data), so no separate list is needed for them.
137	need_build=0
138	for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}" "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
139	  fixture=""
140	  for tok in ${entry#*|}; do
141	    case "$tok" in FIXTURE=*) fixture="${tok#FIXTURE=}" ;; esac
142	  done
143	  if [[ -n "$fixture" && ! -e "$TEST_DIR/$fixture.elf" ]]; then
144	    need_build=1
145	  fi
146	done
147	if (( need_build )); then
148	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
149	  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
150	fi
151	
152	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
153	case "$MODE" in
154	  marker|pc|both) ;;
155	  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
156	esac
157	
158	default_jobs() {
159	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
160	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
161	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
162	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
163	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
164	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
165	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
166	    fi
167	  fi
168	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
169	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
170	}
171	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
172	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
173	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
174	
175	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
176	
177	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
178	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
179	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
180	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
181	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
182	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
183	
184	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
185	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
186	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
187	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
188	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
189	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
190	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
191	run_one() {
192	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
193	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
194	  local start end elapsed status rc
195	  start=$(date +%s)
196	  set +e
197	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
198	  rc=$?
199	  set -e
200	  end=$(date +%s)
201	  elapsed=$((end - start))
202	  case $rc in
203	    0)  status=PASS ;;
204	    77) status=SKIP ;;
205	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
206	  esac
207	  (
208	    flock 9
209	    case "$status" in
210	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
211	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
212	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
213	    esac
214	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
215	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
216	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
217	}
218	
219	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
220	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
221	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
222	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
223	for tm in marker pc; do
224	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
225	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
226	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
227	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
228	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
229	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
230	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
231	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
232	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
233	  done
234	done
235	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
236	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
237	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
238	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
239	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
240	done
241	
242	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
243	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
244	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
245	for tm in marker pc; do
246	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
247	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
248	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
249	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
250	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
251	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
252	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
253	  done
254	done
255	
256	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
257	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
258	
259	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
260	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
261	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
262	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
263	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
264	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
265	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
266	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
267	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
268	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
269	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
270	  printf '.\n' >&8
271	done
272	
273	i=0
274	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
275	  i=$((i+1))
276	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
277	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
278	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
279	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
280	  read -r -u 8 _tok
281	  (
282	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
283	    printf '.\n' >&8
284	  ) &
285	done
286	wait
287	exec 8>&-
288	
289	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
290	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
291	  i=$((i+1))
292	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
293	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
294	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
295	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
296	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
297	done
298	
299	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
300	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
301	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
302	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
303	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
304	  case "$r_status" in
305	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
306	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
307	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
308	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
309	  esac
310	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
311	
312	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
313	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
314	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
315	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
316	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
317	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
318	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
319	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
320	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
321	    echo
322	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
323	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
324	  fi
325	done
326	
327	echo
328	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
329	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
330	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
331	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
332	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
333	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
334	step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
335	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
336	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
337	  exit 1
338	fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium,
#                falling back to the first sim_* only when the canonical
#                engine is not built -- see the comment at the default)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Fill env gaps from ./config.env (the per-host file setup.sh maintains) so
# `scripts/test_all.sh e2e` works from a fresh shell. An exported value wins;
# the file only supplies what the caller's shell lacks -- same pattern as
# tests/lib. Exported for the child builds (make -C tests/fixtures).
cfg_val() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -1; }
for _k in QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 \
          LINUX_TOOLCHAIN; do
  if [[ -z "${!_k:-}" ]]; then
    _v="$(cfg_val "$_k")"
    [[ -n "$_v" ]] && export "$_k=$_v"
  fi
done
unset _k _v

# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
# VSIM_QEMU); empty when neither setup.sh nor config.env supplied it -- the
# require below reports it.
VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_all_fprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_fprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

# Fixture auto-build gate: the required ELF set is DERIVED from the test
# tables above (each entry's FIXTURE= token), so it cannot drift from the
# tests that consume the ELFs. The NEG_TESTS drivers reuse fixtures
# already named in RT_TESTS (handoff_roundtrip, rt_c_dlm_data,
# rt_c_hvm_data), so no separate list is needed for them.
need_build=0
for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}" "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
  fixture=""
  for tok in ${entry#*|}; do
    case "$tok" in FIXTURE=*) fixture="${tok#FIXTURE=}" ;; esac
  done
  if [[ -n "$fixture" && ! -e "$TEST_DIR/$fixture.elf" ]]; then
    need_build=1
  fi
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done

TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
done

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
#             then vlinux
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
#             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
#   vlinux    build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf (the vlinux proxy-kernel
#             skeleton, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md; depends on the runtime
#             lib, built automatically)
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures"; run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
  vlinux)   run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
esac

# rt_csr / rt_csr_survival both match (and any future rt_csr_*). To run

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/e2e.sh must print kernel_cycles -- the vsim mcycle delta over the
# measured region (vsim drain - QEMU1 drain, offset 624) -- for both
# trigger modes (marker, pc), so the `./andesim run --mode hybrid

1 #ifndef ANDESIM_ECALL_HOOK_H
   2 #define ANDESIM_ECALL_HOOK_H
   3 
   4 /* Linux-syscall extension point for the shared M-mode trap handler
   5  * (handler.c). `regs` is trap.S's register-save frame: regs[N] is xN for N
   6  * in {0,1,3..31} (x2/sp is not saved there -- it is the frame pointer
   7  * itself), regs[32]=mepc, regs[33]=mstatus, regs[34]=mxstatus. A handler
   8  * that services the ecall must advance regs[32] past it (+4) before
   9  * returning 1; returning 0 means "not handled", which falls through to the
  10  * fatal trap diagnostic (handler.c's existing behavior for every payload
  11  * that does not override this hook).
  12  *
  13  * handler.c defines a weak default (always 0), so every payload except
  14  * vlinux (which never issues `ecall`) is unaffected by this hook's
  15  * existence. vlinux's runtime/linux/syscall.c provides the strong
  16  * definition (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3).
  17  */
  18 int handle_ecall(unsigned long* regs);
  19 
  20 #endif /* ANDESIM_ECALL_HOOK_H */
=== main.c ===
   1 /* vlinux: boot, banner, manifest reader (U1); ELF loader + Linux initial
   2  * stack + auxv (U3); the syscall core -- brk/mmap-backed malloc + the
   3  * "Set 1" ecall dispatch a static glibc needs to reach main() (U4,
   4  * mm.c/syscall.c).
   5  *
   6  * crt0.o (shared with vplat, see ../crt0.S) has already enabled the
   7  * icache/dcache, mstatus.FS/VS and mmisc_ctl.UNA, and installed the
   8  * fatal-trap handler before calling here.
   9  */
  10 
  11 #include <stddef.h>
  12 #include <stdint.h>
  13 #include <stdio.h>
  14 
  15 #include "loader.h"
  16 #include "manifest.h"
  17 #include "mm.h"
  18 #include "stack.h"
  19 
  20 /* const volatile: the C program never writes this (const), but its true
  21  * value comes from a post-link `objcopy --update-section` binary patch
  22  * (U2), invisible to the compiler -- without `volatile`, -O1 constant-folds
  23  * every read back to the empty-string initializer below and vlinux never
  24  * notices a manifested app_path. */
  25 __attribute__((section(".manifest"), used)) const volatile struct
  26   vlinux_manifest g_manifest = {
  27     .magic = VLINUX_MANIFEST_MAGIC,
  28     .version = VLINUX_MANIFEST_VERSION,
  29     .mem_size = 1024ull * 1024 * 1024,
  30     .app_path = "",
  31     .ram_base = 0, /* v3: flat-from-zero, the historical map */
  32   };
  33 
  34 /* Set sp and jump to the app's entry point. Never returns -- the app runs
  35  * with vlinux's own C stack gone, so there is nothing left to return to. */
  36 static void __attribute__((noreturn)) enter_app(uintptr_t sp, uintptr_t entry)
  37 {
  38   /* load_elf() wrote the app's code via ordinary guest stores (through the
  39    * D-cache crt0.S enabled); without fence.i those writes are not
  40    * guaranteed visible to instruction fetch -- on a real cached core (unlike
  41    * QEMU's cacheless functional model, where this was silently a no-op) the
  42    * hart can fetch stale/empty I-cache lines instead of the just-written
  43    * code. Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes then executes
  44    * new code, not a workaround for this engine specifically. */
  45   asm volatile("fence.i\n"
  46                "mv sp, %0\n"
  47                "jr %1\n"
  48                :
  49                : "r"(sp), "r"(entry)
  50                : "memory");
  51   for (;;)
  52     ; /* unreachable */
  53 }
  54 
  55 int main(void)
  56 {
  57   /* Snapshot the volatile-qualified fields into plain locals once, so
  58    * loader.c/stack.c (which know nothing about the manifest's storage) see
  59    * ordinary, unqualified parameter types. */
  60   char app_path[sizeof(g_manifest.app_path)];
  61   for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(app_path); ++i) app_path[i] = g_manifest.app_path[i];
  62   const uint64_t mem_size = g_manifest.mem_size;
  63   const uint64_t ram_base = g_manifest.ram_base; /* v3/U10d; 0 == v2 layout */
  64   const uint32_t argv_extra_count = g_manifest.argv_extra_count;
  65   char argv_extra_buf[sizeof(g_manifest.argv_extra_buf)];
  66   for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(argv_extra_buf); ++i)
  67     argv_extra_buf[i] = g_manifest.argv_extra_buf[i];
  68 
  69   if (app_path[0] == '\0') {
  70     printf("vlinux: boot ok mem=%uM\n", (unsigned) (mem_size >> 20));
  71     return 0;
  72   }
  73 
  74   struct loaded_elf elf;
  75   if (load_elf(app_path, ram_base, mem_size, &elf) != 0) {
  76     printf("vlinux: failed to load %s\n", app_path);
  77     return 1;
  78   }
  79   mm_init(elf.image_end, ram_base, mem_size);
  80 
  81   const uintptr_t sp = build_initial_stack(app_path, ram_base, mem_size, &elf,
  82                                            argv_extra_buf, argv_extra_count);
  83   enter_app(sp, (uintptr_t) elf.entry);
  84 }

# Linux-Runtime Roadmap: run static glibc binaries (llama.cpp) on andesim

Goal: a prebuilt RISC-V **static glibc** binary (built with the Andes
`nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d` toolchain) runs on every andesim mode
(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid
measures ONE kernel iteration (marker or PC trigger) on vsim. Primary
target: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI, `tools/completion/`
in `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp`) generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`.

How: a small M-mode **proxy kernel** (`vlinux.elf`, new `runtime/linux/`
component, pattern: riscv-pk) that loads the app ELF, builds the Linux
initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and answers the app's `ecall`s by
emulating ~30 Linux syscalls on top of the existing HTIF syscall window.
The hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need
NO changes: the guest stays bare-metal, M-mode, paging-off, single-hart,
exactly the current ROI envelope.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope here)
- No real Linux kernel boot, no S/U-mode, no paging, no interrupts
  (that is FRS FR-109, a separate track).
- No threads: `clone` returns -ENOSYS; llama.cpp runs with `-t 1`
  (verified: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls pthread_create, and
  uncontended glibc mutexes never reach futex).
- No dynamic linking: the app must be `-static` (the toolchain ships
  `libc.a`; a static hello links at vaddr 0x50000, inside DRAM).
- Full 3.8 GB Bonsai-27B residency is blocked by the 2 GiB DRAM window;
  that lift is feature U10 (platform track). Until then use a
  layer-sliced GGUF (U11) - per-layer kernel shapes are identical.
  NOT on the critical path: the primary target Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
  (572 MB) fits the 2 GiB window directly, no slicing needed. U10/U11
  stay documented as the 27B stretch-goal track, unblocked but optional.

Verified facts this design stands on (probed 2026-07-15)

## U10. Platform track: guest RAM > 2 GiB (full Bonsai-27B) [stretch, off critical path]

Rescoped 2026-07-29 after measuring the real blockers. The original U10 text
said three things that are now wrong or answered:
- (1) "qemu_andesim DRAM window (currently Cannot model more than 2GB)" is
  **DONE upstream**. `hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:73,131,132` now defines
  `DRAM` 0x0 +2 GiB, `DRAM_ALIAS` 0x8_00000000 +2 GiB (aliases DRAM), and
  `DRAM_EXT` 0x8_80000000 +14 GiB; the error at :1814-1823 reads "Cannot
  model more than 16GB RAM". :974-981 auto-enables the alias when
  `ram_size > DRAM.size` precisely so ext RAM is reachable **contiguously
  from 0x8_00000000**, and :1837-1850 maps ONE `machine->ram` backend across
  both windows via aliases -- so hybrid's `memory-backend-file` already
  spans them. Nothing to do in QEMU.
- (2) "is the vsim testbench memory parameterizable?" -> **yes, in hybrid
  mode it already is.** `vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:458-465`: when
  `--shared-mem-path` is given, the RAM region is exactly
  `{shared_mem_base, shared_mem_base + shared_mem_size - 1}` with no
  hardcoded 2 GiB. `SimpleMemory<BusWidth>` (src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:14-18)
  takes 32 = bus width in BYTES, not address bits; addresses are u64
  throughout. So the vsim side likely needs NO code change -- U10a verifies.
- (3) "the vlinux arena bounds (already mem_size-driven)" is **the actual

LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000

# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
GLIBC_CC = $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     rt_linux_argv.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

rt_linux_argv.elf: rt_linux_argv.c
	$(CC) $(LINUX_APP_CFLAGS) $(LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS) $< -o $@

# Static-glibc app fixtures sharing one toolchain/link (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md):
#   rt_linux_glibc_hello  U4: hello world
#   rt_linux_file         U5: file I/O syscall set
#   rt_linux_time         U6: time syscalls
#   rt_linux_mmap         U7: file-backed private mmap
# NOT part of `all` -- they need the optional LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (env-gated, like
# the rv32 fixtures need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32). Build individually:
# make rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf
RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES := rt_linux_glibc_hello rt_linux_file rt_linux_time \
                           rt_linux_mmap
$(RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9: marker'd glibc kernel under hybrid. Same
# toolchain/link, plus the installed andesim/ROI.h include path (the same
# runtime/ build every vplat fixture uses via -B/-specs -- this fixture
# just needs the ONE header, not the whole bare-metal runtime).
rt_linux_matvec.elf: rt_linux_matvec.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall \
	  -I $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include $< -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
