#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --mem-size contract: one model-neutral flag, per-model semantics, plus the
# hybrid V-scratch boundary.
#
#   fast:   forwards --mem-size verbatim to QEMU's `-m`; QEMU itself validates
#           its DRAM ceiling (this AE350 build tops out at 16 GiB). A non-whole-
#           MiB size is rejected by the driver first.
#   hybrid: sizes the shared mmap (= QEMU backend = vsim window). The driver
#           reserves ONE V-scratch page ABOVE program RAM, so the usable window
#           is the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM window MINUS that page. Exactly 2G therefore
#           overflows and is rejected; 2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that
#           fits. See driver/shm.cpp max_program_mem_bytes().
#   cycle:  validate-only (the engine always models its full DRAM window).
#   --mmap-size stays a hidden alias of --mem-size.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"        # engine-portable (fast/cycle)
MELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"        # carries ROI markers (hybrid)
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium

require_driver

==> /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_mmap2g.sh <==
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Max-window proof for the hybrid shared mmap. The largest --mem-size the driver
# allows is 2047 MiB: the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM window MINUS the one V-scratch page
# the driver parks on top (exactly 2G is rejected -- see the memsize test). This
# runs at that maximum: phase 1 (QEMU) writes a pattern into the LAST page of
# program RAM (0x7FEFF000, immediately below the V-scratch page at 0x7FF00000)
# and the ROI (vsim) reads it back through the shared mmap. Passing means the
# whole stack -- driver cap, sparse backing file, QEMU memory backend, vsim RAM
# window -- agrees on the same near-2-GiB window end to end.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null || true
GCC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

require_driver
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "SKIP: no riscv toolchain"; exit 0; }
[ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime" ] || { echo "SKIP: vplat runtime not built"; exit 0; }

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t mmap2g.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

==> /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh <==
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the andesim runtime builds for BOTH arches from two
# toolchains. ARCH=rv64 (default) -> build/runtime/, ARCH=rv32 -> build/runtime/rv32/.
# The produced objects must be the right ELF class (rv64=ELFCLASS64, rv32=ELFCLASS32).
#
#   rv64 always runs (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32; SKIPs if unset.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val

elf_class() { od -An -j4 -N1 -tu1 "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '; }   # 1=ELF32 2=ELF64

TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC64" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"

# rv64 (default ARCH): library + crt0 land in build/runtime and are ELFCLASS64.
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv64 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC64" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv64 runtime build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: missing build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/crt0.o")" = "2" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS64"
ok "rv64 runtime -> build/runtime (ELFCLASS64)"

#   rv64 always runs (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32; SKIPs if unset.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val

elf_class() { od -An -j4 -N1 -tu1 "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '; }   # 1=ELF32 2=ELF64

TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC64" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"

# rv64 (default ARCH): library + crt0 land in build/runtime and are ELFCLASS64.
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv64 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC64" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv64 runtime build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: missing build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/crt0.o")" = "2" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS64"
ok "rv64 runtime -> build/runtime (ELFCLASS64)"

1a44ca1 feat(runtime): U10c+U10d - host-testable RAM math, manifest v3 ram_base (structural+behavioral)
commit 1a44ca175554b58b69469e192ea5c533db181458
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Tue Aug 4 17:46:46 2026 +0800

    feat(runtime): U10c+U10d - host-testable RAM math, manifest v3 ram_base (structural+behavioral)
    
    Committed as one unit because the two features share edits in mm.c/stack.c/
    loader.c; each is individually documented DONE in ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md.
    
    U10c (structural): extract vlinux's four size->address computations into pure
    functions in runtime/linux/vlinux_mem.h (vlinux_ram_top, vlinux_mmap_arena_top,
    vlinux_v_scratch_base); VLINUX_STACK_RESERVE moves there so mm.c and stack.c
    structurally cannot desynchronize. New driver/vlinux_mem_test.cpp (14th driver
    test) pins today's ram_base==0 answers and encodes the 3G trap-storm bug as an
    assertion on the unmapped-hole address.
    
    U10d (behavioral): vlinux_manifest gains uint64_t ram_base (version 2 -> 3);
    threaded through mm_init, build_initial_stack, load_elf, build_manifest_blob,
    stage_linux_runtime. The driver still passes ram_base = 0, so the guest layout
    is byte-for-byte v2's - flipping it on is U10e/U10f.
    
    Also: docs updates (USER_GUIDE, llama_roi_howto) and
    scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh, the documented K=51 hybrid example runner.
    
    14/14 driver unit tests green.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

 docs/USER_GUIDE.md          |   9 ++
